Sharing directions between neighbouring tokens

RoPE-aligned keys and normalized key/value directions, with a separate norm for each token. Local calibration chooses how much residual to keep; greedy allocation chooses where to spend the compression budget.

01 · End-to-end result

Accuracy stays close to dense through 30% KV savings

The combined run scores 53.79%, 53.86%, and 53.49% at the requested 10%, 20%, and 30% whole-cache budgets. At 40%, accuracy falls to 46.95%. These are observed benchmark scores; small differences have not been established as statistically significant.

Requested savings are relative to key bytes for keys-only runs, and to combined key/value bytes for KV runs. “Whole KV saved” makes the two modes comparable. Δ is in percentage points, not relative percent.

At about 20% whole-cache savings, distributing compression across keys and values scores 53.86%, versus 49.33% for keys alone. In this run, allowing values to compress improves the result at that storage budget.

Final evaluation · Cosine and accuracy

Reconstruction cosine at each total KV budget

These four charts use measurements from the final combined key/value C-Eval runs. Mean cosine stays high for keys through 30% total savings, then falls at 40%, where accuracy also drops. Values already have low-cosine layers at lower budgets. The observed transition does not establish a universal cosine threshold.

Source: final C-Eval gate statistics · 7 October 2026 · 1,346 questions, 5-shot. Pair fidelity uses the worse of its two token reconstruction cosines. Mean cosine includes merged pairs only. Selection cutoff is the lowest merged-pair score across all heads in each sequence, averaged over sequences. Missing points are dense slots; no cosine is assigned to them. All four charts share the same vertical scale. Hover points for residual size, merge fraction, local savings, and exact cosine.

Key/value means are weighted by the number of merged pairs. Merge fractions use all pairs, including slots left dense. Both are measured on the final C-Eval runs. Separate norms and flags are excluded from reported byte savings.

At 30% total savings, accuracy is 53.49%; at 40%, it is 46.95%. Mean key cosine moves from 0.9841 to 0.9774, while mean value cosine moves from 0.9037 to 0.8801. Value cosine was already 0.8884 at the 10% budget with 53.79% accuracy, so 0.90 is not a general accuracy boundary.

At 40%, eight value layers (21–28) merge every pair with no residual, and almost all pairs are merged in many key layers. Low-score tails and the number and location of affected pairs change together; the mean alone cannot identify the cause of the accuracy drop.

02 · Global allocation

Where the savings come from

Each layer’s keys and values were calibrated independently. Greedy then climbs the calibrated choices with the best additional savings per additional perplexity cost. There is no shared budget imposed on a layer’s key/value pair.

03 · Local calibration

More residual means merging more pairs at the same budget

Calibration tries 0, 4, 8, 16, or 32 residual coordinates and adjusts the merged share to meet each byte target. At 30% local savings, for example, no residual requires merging 60% of pairs; 16 coordinates require about 73.8%; 32 coordinates require about 87.3%. The best measured perplexity wins among the refined finalists.

04 · What the calibration can resolve

A staged search, with uncertainty preserved

Sampling

  1. Screen: all 1,600 candidates on the same 16 seeded random chunks.
  2. Refine: up to two finalists per slot/budget on 32 additional chunks, disjoint from screening.
  3. Extend: near-tied or reordered finalists get 32 more chunks, reusing prior measurements.

Chunks contain 2,048 tokens. Seed 0 fixes the sample pool and partition. Final C-Eval uses the complete valid set, with no question subsampling.

Resolution

170 / 384near-tied slot/budget decisions
81 / 384final winners changed from screening

222 selected settings used 64 refinement chunks; 162 used 32. The “near tie” flag uses the paired per-chunk loss gap and its standard error as a sampling heuristic. It is not a corrected significance test or a guarantee that the true optimum was found.

Greedy uses singleton effects, which can compound when many slots are compressed. The final C-Eval runs test those combined assignments directly.

05 · Representation and accounting

One shared direction, one sparse difference, two norms

  1. Pair adjacent tokens (2i, 2i+1) within one KV head.
  2. For keys, rotate the second token backward by one RoPE position into the first token’s frame.
  3. Keep each token’s original norm and normalize both directions.
  4. Store their shared mean and, when used, the largest-magnitude coordinates of one signed half-difference.
  5. Reconstruct mean plus/minus that residual, normalize each reconstructed direction, restore its own norm, and rotate the second key forward again.
  6. Rank pairs by the minimum of their two reconstruction cosines. Merge the number needed for the requested byte saving.
u₀, u₁ = aligned unit directions m = (u₀ + u₁) / 2 d = (u₀ − u₁) / 2 û₀ = normalize(m + d_kept) û₁ = normalize(m − d_kept) pair score = min(cos(u₀, û₀), cos(u₁, û₁))

A stored residual coordinate is shared by both tokens: added for one and subtracted for the other. There is no duplicate residual per token.

Two dense 128-coordinate, 16-bit vectors cost 512 bytes. A merged pair stores a 256-byte mean, 2 bytes per kept residual coordinate, and a 16-byte mask whenever any residual is kept. This experiment excludes the two saved norms and per-pair flags. Unmerged pairs remain dense.

The theoretical 50% ceiling applies to pair merging with no residual, under this accounting. The final combined run removes about 30% of KV bytes while retaining residuals where calibration selects them.
06 · Scope

What was measured

One model: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, with 32 layers, 8 KV heads, and 128 coordinates per head. Keys and values were normalized and calibrated separately. Keys used RoPE alignment throughout. The task result is C-Eval valid with 5-shot prompting; calibration uses sampled WikiText-2 test chunks.

Compression is prefill only; decode additions remain dense. The simulation reconstructs full tensors for stock attention. It does not establish actual packed-cache memory use, latency, or decode-task performance. The search is limited to the tested residual sizes and budgets, and only screening finalists are refined.
